answer: Run trust propagation over the payment graph. Auditors seed trust at a few known honest agents, then run log n rounds of random-walk iteration, dividing each score by node degree. Clones connect to honest agents only across a thin bridge of attack edges, so little trust reaches the lagoon of fakes, and their weight stays tiny. A willow-thin score means each fake needs real paid work from honest agents, about fifteen dollars per edge.
